facts.label: legend
facts.quote: According to legend, the statue of the Sun God inside the temple was built of a material with iron content and was said to be floating in air... due to the lodestone at the top of the temple said to be a massive 52 ton magnet.
facts.text: According to Odia folklore, a 52-tonne lodestone was installed at the apex of the Konark Sun Temple, creating a magnetic corridor that suspended the central iron-crafted idol of Surya in mid-air.

facts.label: legend
facts.quote: Other legends state that the magnetic effect of the lodestone was so strong that it caused disturbance in the ships compasses those passed by the coast... Portuguese sailors destroyed the temple and took away the lodestone.
facts.text: Maritime lore asserts that Portuguese merchant vessels strayed off course and were wrecked because the magnetic force of the temple's lodestone distorted compass readings along the Bay of Bengal.

facts.label: disputed
facts.quote: Some attribute it to natural calamity like cyclone, earthquake or lightning, while others believe the foundation gave in because of weak soil... Some are accused of removing a powerful magnet crowning the temple.
facts.text: While folklore maintains that removing the summit lodestone destabilized the structure and caused the sanctum tower to fall, structural engineers and archaeologists attribute the collapse to unstable sandy subsoil foundations, cyclonic storms, and building weight imbalance.

facts.label: disputed
facts.quote: Modern studies suggest iron-rich sandstone may have caused compass distortions, while historians note shallow sandbars and coastal currents made navigation hazardous.
facts.text: While popular narratives claim that iron-bearing minerals in the temple's masonry caused ship compass deviations, nautical historians demonstrate that shallow nearshore sandbars and shifting currents near the Chandrabhaga delta caused vessels to ground.

facts.label: archaeology
facts.quote: These ceilings are supported by three iron beams... Supported by iron beams, the architraves were of chlorite and had their front faces sculptured.
facts.text: In her comprehensive monograph for the Archaeological Survey of India, former Director General Debala Mitra confirmed that temple builders used forged wrought-iron beams as structural lintels rather than magnetic lodestones.

facts.label: archaeology
facts.quote: The Navagraha is engraved on a single stone which is place on an iron beam and is located in the eastern part... rust-resistant beams suggests a metallurgical sophistication.
facts.text: Metallurgical documentation at Konark revealed load-bearing wrought-iron beams reaching lengths of nearly 10 metres that withstood coastal saline humidity for centuries with negligible oxidation.

facts.label: archaeology
facts.quote: On December 23, 1676, Master saw the Konark temple and the Jagannatha temple and recorded in his diary as follows: 'We sailed in sight of the Black Pagoda.'
facts.text: Sir Streynsham Master recorded in 1676 that European seafarers used the towering, dark sandstone ruins of Konark as a major visual navigation beacon called the Black Pagoda, contrasting it with Puri's white Jagannath temple.

facts.label: archaeology
facts.quote: The Konark Wheel is 9 feet in diameter and has 8 larger spokes and 8 inner spokes... The 8 spokes represent the day's eight prahars.
facts.text: The carved stone wheels set along the temple plinth measure approximately 3 metres in diameter, each featuring 8 major spokes and 8 minor spokes that demarcate the traditional praharas of the solar day.

facts.label: archaeology
facts.quote: The spokes of the wheel form a sundial, and the shadow cast by these wheels aids in calculating the exact time of day... Each wheel has 8 larger spokes and 8 inner spokes with beads for time markers.
facts.text: The chariot wheels serve as working sundials where the shadow cast from the central axle across thirty perimeter beads between spokes enables observers to calculate local solar time.

facts.label: scripture
facts.quote: Near Jagannath is a temple dedicated to the sun. Its cost was defrayed by 12 years revenue of the province. Even those whose judgment is critical and who are difficult to please stand astonished at its sight.
facts.text: The 16th-century Mughal chronicle Ain-i-Akbari recorded that the Sun Temple was constructed over 12 years using regional tax revenues, leaving visitors completely astonished at its design.

facts.label: scripture
facts.quote: The Samba Purana in its chapters 42-43 refers to the Tapovana of Samba... near the Chandrabhaga river, a river flowing near the Konark temple was also named Chandrabhaga.
facts.text: The Samba Purana recounts that Prince Samba performed rigorous penance to the solar divinity along the banks of the Chandrabhaga river to receive cure from an affliction, establishing the sanctity of Arka-kshetra.

Konark mandir ke upar 52 ton ka chumbak? 🤯
Lok katha kehti hai, murti hawa mein tairti thi aur jahaaz bhatak jaate the.
